subtype: Approach: sets a review point in advance to decide whether to continue [Action]
passage:
In the kasba engineering college hostel, Baljeet was starting a small app that shows bus timings for the town. Before he wrote a single line, he took a page and wrote: "Review on 15 September. If fewer than fifty people use it, I stop and spend the time on placement preparation." He pinned it above his desk and showed Suraj, his roommate. "Hold me to it."

Three months later, on the fifteenth, they opened the counter together. Nineteen users. Baljeet looked at it for a long time, then closed the laptop. "That was the deal." He felt a little heavy, but the next morning he opened the aptitude book at page one. The page above the desk stayed where it was.

qa.q: How many users did the app have on the review day?
How did Baljeet feel when he closed the laptop?
qa.a: Baljeet felt a little heavy and disappointed, but accepted it because it was the deal.

qa.q: What could Baljeet do to keep the lessons from the project?
qa.a: Baljeet could write down what he learned about users and about building the app, to use in later projects or placement interviews.

qa.q: How might Suraj see holding Baljeet to the rule?
qa.a: Suraj might feel awkward but supportive, since Baljeet asked for it and the rule was set in advance.

grounding: Shows a student setting a review point in advance and stopping the side project when the target is missed.

subtype: Approach: sets a review point in advance to decide whether to continue [Action]
passage: In his second year at university in Osaka, Kaito started building a small app for sharing lecture notes. His friend Camila asked how long he'd keep at it. Kaito opened his calendar and put a reminder on the date exactly three months away: "Review: 50 users?" Under it he wrote, "If no, stop and use evenings for interview practice." Then he got to work. He built the first version, posted it on the student board, handed out flyers. At the end of month two, he had eleven users, mostly friends. On the review date, he had fourteen. He sat with his tea, looked at the number, and closed the project folder. That evening he emailed the careers office to book a mock interview.

qa.q: How many users did Kaito have on the review date?
How might Kaito have felt closing the project folder?
qa.a: He probably felt disappointed but also relieved and clear, because the decision had been made in advance.

qa.q: Which choice helped Kaito most, and why?
qa.a: Setting the review date and the 50-user target at the start, so stopping was a plan, not a painful argument with himself.

qa.q: How might Camila see Kaito's decision?
qa.a: Camila may be impressed that he kept his own rule, instead of carrying on out of pride.

grounding: A student sets a three-month review point for a side project and stops for placement preparation when users do not appear.

subtype: Approach: sets a review point in advance to decide whether to continue [Action]
passage: In the engineering hostel, Vikas pinned a paper to his door in August: "Campus snacks website. Review on 30 November. Target: 40 regular users. Below that, stop and switch to placement prep." His roommate Yash read it and laughed. "Very official." Vikas spent his evenings coding, took photos of the canteen menus and posted the link in every hostel group. By October, six people used it. On 30 November, Vikas sat at the hostel reading room table with the numbers: nine users. He sighed, rubbed his eyes, then crossed out the paper on his door and wrote underneath: "Stopped. Placement prep from 1 December." Yash helped him make an aptitude-practice timetable that night.

qa.q: What was Vikas's target for regular users?
What did Vikas's sigh and rubbed eyes suggest?
qa.a: He felt disappointed and tired, but he kept his rule, which suggests he was also settled about the choice.

qa.q: What could Vikas do with what he built?
qa.a: Share the code or idea with a junior who might grow it, while he focuses on placement prep.

qa.q: How does Yash see the plan by the end?
qa.a: Yash went from teasing to helping, likely respecting that Vikas stuck to the review point.

grounding: A student sets a fixed review date for a side project and switches to placement preparation when the users do not come.
